subject: ইংরেজি লিখিত
question: As a Sub-Assistant Maintenance Engineer, write a formal 'Technical Incident & Downtime Report' addressed to the System Analyst regarding a major network outage at the Regional Technical School and College (TSC) / Polytechnic Institute caused by a broadcast storm/switching loop. Outline root cause, immediate recovery actions, and long-term preventive measures.
answer:
Model Technical Incident Report:

TECHNICAL INCIDENT REPORT

Reference: DIP/RPO-DHK/INC-2026/089
Date: 23 October 2026
To: System Analyst, ICT Division, Department of Immigration & Passports
From: Sub-Assistant Maintenance Engineer, Regional Technical School and College (TSC) / Polytechnic Institute
Subject: Incident Post-Mortem Report: 90-Minute Network Downtime at Enrollment LAN

1. Executive Summary:
On 23 October 2026 at 10:15 AM, the local area network (LAN) serving all 14 biometric enrollment counters and the citizen queue display system experienced a total outage. Normal operations were fully restored by 11:45 AM (total downtime: 90 minutes).

2. Incident Timeline & Symptoms:
• 10:15 AM: Enrollment workstations reported disconnection from the local verification server; network latency spiked above 4,000 ms with 95% packet drop.
• 10:30 AM: Physical inspection of the core distribution switch (Cisco Catalyst 2960X) revealed 100% CPU utilization and simultaneous flashing of all port activity LEDs (classic broadcast storm indicator).

3. Root Cause Analysis:
An unauthorized patch cord was accidentally cross-connected between two access ports on Switch Rack-02 during routine desk rearrangement by floor support staff. Because Spanning Tree Protocol (STP) BPDU Guard was globally disabled on access-layer edge ports, an active Layer-2 loop formed instantly, generating overwhelming broadcast traffic.

4. Immediate Remediation:
• The redundant looping patch cable was identified and physically disconnected at 10:50 AM.
• Switch CPU loads normalized within 3 minutes; all core IP services and DHCP leases were validated.
• All 14 client workstations successfully resumed biometric enrollment and MRZ submissions by 11:45 AM.

5. Corrective & Preventive Measures:
• Globally enabled Rapid Spanning Tree Protocol (RSTP) with PortFast and BPDU Guard on all client-facing switch ports.
• Physically locked unused RJ-45 wall ports using port blockers to prevent unauthorized interconnects.
• Scheduled a technical refresher session on rack cabling protocols for support personnel.

Submitted by:
(Signature)
Md. Rafiqul Islam
Sub-Assistant Maintenance Engineer
points_to_remember: Follow standard BPSC/technical incident report structure: Executive Summary, Timeline, Root Cause, Immediate Remediation, and Preventive Action.
Use authentic networking concepts: Switching loop, Broadcast storm, Cisco 2960X, RSTP, BPDU Guard.

question: Draft a comprehensive 'Network Incident & Root Cause Analysis (RCA) Report' addressed to the Director (ICT) concerning an unexpected core distribution switch failure that caused a 45-minute outage at the central passport issuance division.
answer:
Network Incident Report:

**DEPARTMENT OF IMMIGRATION & PASSPORTS**
**ICT & INFRASTRUCTURE WING, HEADQUARTERS, DHAKA**

**INCIDENT REPORT & ROOT CAUSE ANALYSIS (RCA)**

**Incident Reference:** INC-2026-1023-NET-01
**Date of Report:** October 23, 2026
**To:** Director (ICT), Department of Immigration and Passports
**From:** Sub-Assistant Maintenance Engineer, Network & Data Center Operations
**Classification:** Severity-1 (High Impact)

**1. Executive Summary:**
On October 23, 2026, at 10:15 AM, the Central Passport Personalization Division experienced an unexpected network outage lasting 45 minutes (10:15 AM to 11:00 AM). The outage temporarily halted passport printing and personalization queuing. Service was fully restored at 11:00 AM following emergency hardware bypass.

**2. Incident Timeline:**
• **10:15 AM:** Core Distribution Switch (Cisco Catalyst 9500) abruptly rebooted and entered a boot-loop.
• **10:18 AM:** Monitoring system (Zabbix) raised high-priority alerts regarding unreachable subnets (VLAN 30 & VLAN 40).
• **10:25 AM:** Maintenance engineers inspected the rack and observed redundant power supply failure (PSU-2 dead, PSU-1 overheating trip).
• **10:35 AM:** Hot-standby switch was configured, and primary fiber uplinks were patched to the redundant switch.
• **10:50 AM:** Spanning-tree protocol (RSTP) converged; database connectivity re-established.
• **11:00 AM:** Full verification completed; all personalization lines resumed normal operation.

**3. Root Cause Analysis (RCA):**
The primary root cause was an internal capacitor breakdown within Power Supply Unit 2 (PSU-2), which produced a power surge that tripped the thermal protection sensor of PSU-1. The automatic hardware failover failed because PSU-1 drew excessive thermal load due to dust accumulation in the secondary fan chassis.

**4. Corrective and Preventive Actions (CAPA):**
1. Replaced both faulty power supply modules with genuine OEM redundant units.
2. Implemented active dual-bus UPS power feeds (Feed A from Online UPS-1, Feed B from Online UPS-2).
3. Scheduled bi-weekly physical air-flow and temperature inspections across all core distribution racks.
4. Configured SNMP trap alerting for switch fan RPM and PSU thermal fluctuations.

**Submitted by:**
*(Signature)*
Sub-Assistant Maintenance Engineer
Department of Immigration and Passports
points_to_remember: An Incident Report must have standard headings: Executive Summary, Timeline, Root Cause Analysis (RCA), and Corrective & Preventive Actions (CAPA).
